question: Can a fixed 24-site full-history register decoder recover distant values faster and with less peak memory than ordinary Base by replacing global attention layer 7 with a second native GDN layer 6?
protocol: Freeze the existing language model, learned register router, attention reader and trained LoRA factors. On register requests only use layers 0 through 23 with site 7 replaced by the second application of layer 6 and residual alpha .35. Native independent full state at every executed site. Five full attention sites preserve keys and values for every input token. Two fixed-position key swaps, 16K and 32K. Use the first legal fixed-width swap per seed series in publisher format. Untouched Base uses six full-attention sites. Alternate first model per request. Record TTFT, actual elapsed seconds, peak allocated MLX bytes, free completions and located spans.
gate: Require 4/4 candidate answers and correctly located spans, more correct than Base, aggregate TTFT at most 95% of Base, total seconds and peak bytes no higher than Base. A pass licenses a separate physical 131K comparison. Failure closes long promotion for this graph.
